title: Improving Group Robustness on Spurious Correlation via Evidential Alignment

problem.claim: Deep neural networks can rely on spurious correlations, achieving high overall accuracy while degrading on diverse scenarios where those correlations do not hold, which challenges out-of-distribution robustness and trustworthiness.

gap.claim: Existing approaches typically require costly external group annotations or auxiliary deterministic models that may not capture the full spectrum of learned biases.

contributions.claim: Evidential Alignment uses uncertainty quantification to understand biased-model behavior without group annotations.
The framework combines second-order risk minimization with evidential calibration to identify and suppress spurious correlations while preserving core features.
The authors theoretically justify learning biased-model patterns and debiasing without spurious-correlation annotations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Evidential Alignment as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significant improvements in group robustness across diverse architectures and data modalities.
The authors characterize the method as scalable and principled for addressing spurious correlations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Models learn superficial non-causal associations, such as identifying camels from desert backgrounds.
Spurious correlations can produce high training accuracy but poor generalization and reduced trustworthiness.
Existing mitigation methods depend on costly group annotations or potentially incomplete deterministic bias models.
Evidential Alignment uses uncertainty quantification, second-order risk minimization, and evidential calibration to suppress spurious correlations without annotations.
The authors report theoretical justification and empirical robustness improvements across architectures and data modalities.
